subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WebSocket origin gate reusing checkBrowserOrigin

question: Should every gateway WebSocket request carrying an Origin be subject to `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` before the client type is known, even when current main only enforces that policy for browser UI, webchat, or explicit all-client enforcement?
rationale: The pre-upgrade `ws` hook runs before OpenClaw receives the connect metadata needed to preserve the current policy boundary, so this is a security/product compatibility choice rather than a mechanical relocation.

options.title: Preserve client-aware admission
options.body: Do not add an unconditional `verifyClient` origin rejection; retain the current post-connect enforcement until an upgrade-safe protocol signal can preserve its scope.

options.title: Adopt an all-Origin gateway policy
options.body: Intentionally reject every Origin-bearing upgrade, document the changed contract, and add compatibility proof for non-UI browser clients plus trusted-proxy paths.

recommendation.title: Preserve client-aware admission
recommendation.body: Do not add an unconditional `verifyClient` origin rejection; retain the current post-connect enforcement until an upgrade-safe protocol signal can preserve its scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the shared origin-check contract makes this person the strongest evidence-backed routing candidate.
